test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A carburetor used in a petrol engine is designed so as to fit in which of the following parts of the engine?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cylinder head**(Option 1)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• A carburetor__ is used in petrol engines to mix air and fuel in the correct proportion for combustion.
 
• It is designed to fit specifically into the cylinder head of the engine.
 
• The carburetor regulates the fuel and air mixture to ensure the engine runs efficiently.
 
• The placement in the cylinder head allows the mixed fuel to be directly injected into the combustion chamber.
 
• Proper functioning of the carburetor is essential for smooth and efficient engine operation.
 
• Modern engines may use fuel injection systems instead of carburetors.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Engine Components:**

 
 
• The cylinder head houses the inlet and exhaust valves, spark plugs, and other parts associated with combustion.
 
• The piston moves inside the cylinder to compress the air-fuel mixture.
 
• The casing provides the housing and framework for the engine components.
 
• The connecting rod links the piston to the crankshaft, converting linear motion into rotational motion.
